d: Pete is in Virginia for a build at the Bella Rose Plantation. Inspired by Thomas Jefferson, he designs a luxurious treehouse with colonial columns.
Pete and his gang ride out to build a double-decker hideout in Texas Hill Country. NT&S creates rustic bliss in six oak trees with a saloon-style first floor.
Tensions rise when Parker introduces a new crew member and a radical plan. The Beets family run an important test on daughter Monica's Hunker Creek claim.
Rick's season is jeopardised when an engineering disaster shuts him down. Parker ploughs big money into a new claim and Tony gets a third operation running.
The Brown family of nine hatches a plan to deal with a lumber shortage, but then a sudden injury threatens to split the family apart.
On the Northwestern, the exhausted crew struggles to keep up with Captain Sig's maniacal pace - and deckhand, Jake Anderson, pays the price in blood.
Game Wardens relocate a large herd of pronghorn to restore its numbers. Plus, they investigate the killing of a protected rattlesnake and wrangle with a loose bull.
At night, Game Wardens are on patrol. They get anonymous tips about anglers fishing over the limit and a specially trained k-9 unit to sniff out illegal items.
How do they handcraft Espadrilles shoes? How do they make prefabricated houses? How they store priceless documents to keep them safe for hundreds of years.
How do they harvest and process the world's toughest and most expensive nut? How do they turn lake water into tap water? How do they hold back fans at gigs.
How do they build the biggest apartment block on the planet? How do they make the classic British boot? How do they make cooking pans last a lifetime.
How do they craft a classic Indian instrument, the Sitar? How do they make beef biltong? Plus, how do they build monster bulldozers.
In Mississippi, the Raneys must first solve the mystery of flooding water before teaching a family of six to thrive off-grid together.
Australia. Mike and Elvis engage in the ultimate Aussie showdown: Ford versus Holden. Can their Ford XR8 outpace the Holden GTS at the Mount Panorama circuit.
Parker's team tries a wild plan to resupply their water. Tony struggles with a rock truck driver. Rick gets test results on his Snake River cut.

Josh braves Nicaragua's croc-infested waters and snake-filled jungle to find the Orus, a ship that crashed in violent rapids on its maiden voyage.
Jessica Chobot and Phil Torres investigate a strange phenomenon that has been haunting Mammoth Cave for generations. What will they discover.
The Cornelia Marie taps American satellites to spy on the Russians while Scott Campbell Jr. pioneers a long-dormant fishery. And, Wild Bill faces big setbacks.

As America marks its 250th birthday, Phil, Heather and Jack Osbourne investigate reports of Revolutionary War ghosts in Pennsylvania.

How do they make the amplifier used by rock legends, the famous Marshall amp? Plus, how do they turn wet clay into frost-proof garden pots.
How do they clean the world's tallest twin towers? How do they make a jigsaw where every piece is unique? How do they craft Olympic level hockey sticks.
How do they fit all the features of a luxury apartment into a motorhome? And, how do they make a ballet shoe that can take the weight of a dancer on tiptoes.
How do they grow nearly 200,000 tonnes of mushrooms a year in the mushroom capital of the world? And, how do they make billions of life-saving gloves.
The duo are challenged to turn an entire Toyota Highlander into an aquarium, while simultaneously opening a new ATM office in South Florida.
The Las Vegas Museum of Natural History asks ATM to create an aquarium in the shape of a carousel, but instead of horses this carousel will be filled with seahorses.
NASCAR And Baseball Champions Tanks! NASCAR champion Ryan Newman gets ATM to make a desk aquarium, and Red Sox star Shane Victorino asks the guys to build a Hawaiian-themed tank.
When the guys are challenged to a Tuff Truck, Sparks Motors rebuilds a wasp-infested old Jeep and the Goons rebuild a water-logged Blazer.
Heavy D and the crew transform a rundown Canadian logging truck into a maxed out, custom semi to transport their builds cross-country.
While the shop finishes the semi build, Heavy D moves ahead with his plan to attempt a death-defying stunt in the Brodozer.
Diesel Air. Heavy D is commissioned to design and build a 1,000-gallon fuel truck and a diesel-powered helicopter bucket to spread fertiliser for a timber business in Oregon.
Heavy D builds two custom fertiliser spreaders and a custom fuel truck for a friend's helicopter business in Oregon. Plus, he picks up a unique Swiss overland camper.
Heavy D continues trying to salvage a wrecked overland camper from Europe, hoping for a big payday. Meanwhile, Sam designs a hub-centric, diesel-powered bicycle.

Chase and his crew help a newlywed couple take a questionable 'wedding gift' and turn it into an alpine ski bungalow that would rival those in the Swiss Alps.
After experiencing a devastating tornado, a family relies on the help of loved ones to build an off-grid retreat overlooking Tennessee's Ocoee River.

To celebrate the series' 20th anniversary, Mike and Elvis set out to restore a Ford Fiesta Mark 1 and stage the show's largest ever car meet.
A Peugeot 205 T16 inspires Mike to upgrade its under-powered UK counterpart for a track race. Can Mike's 205 Rallye compete with a Eurospec Peugeot.
Mike thinks there's money to be made on a soft-top Saab 900, but it's got a dodgy clutch and woolly steering. Can Elvis get it back to its best.
Mike buys his newest ever car to create a bespoke Scooby BRZ STI. But hopes of a profit are hit with a hefty bill for the turbo and a new exhaust.
A nature-loving architect builds a modern cabin in the Californian Redwoods. He faces challenges, but the final project will have views to rival the Big Sur.
An eco-friendly couple are battling against the harsh winter weather to build a timber and straw-bale cabin in Maine. They are building in a heavily wooded forest.
A novice builder tries to construct a stone cabin in Vermont's White River Valley but his inexperience and the harsh winter push him to his limits.
Broken Bridges. Marty responds to a new, desperate plea from the Bower Family in eastern Vermont: a 100-year flood has wiped out their property access route.
The Raneys race winter to build the first ever 'homestead fortress,' and protect a family from brown bears that have taken over a remote homestead.
The Raneys head off to answer an SOS call from an off-grid couple. But with severe storms threatening floods, they are in a race against Mother Nature.
The Raneys try to restore a failed homestead in Ohio. Marty's only hope is an old gas well, which if he can get working, can breathe life back into the property.
The crew rebuilds the Minor Hill cabin in Franklin, Tennessee. Mark Bowe checks out a log cabin added to an 1806 stone home and tours a local whiskey distillery.
Stefan stops a man claiming he's been to Denmark to buy duck, but no duck is to be found among the booze he has brought. At Arlanda a man is furious.

In Hawaii, the Raneys rescue a young family with a crumbling cabin on a homestead infested by slugs carrying a brain-eating parasite.
Australia. Mike and Elvis find a 1970s classic VW camper in need of some mechanical TLC. Can they turn it into a long-range camper fit for the Australian wilderness.
